title: If police or a post-mortem are involved
description: The death was an accident, a suicide, or not clear, and the police are involved.
opening: After an accident, a suicide or a death that is not clear, the law asks the police to make an enquiry.

official.text: When police learn of a suicide, a death caused by another person, an animal, a machine or an accident, or a death that raises suspicion, they tell the nearest Executive Magistrate and go to where the body is.
official.confirms: Delhi Police Academy BNSS Handbook, Section 194(1) BNSS (old CrPC 174), quoted in full.

official.text: There, with two or more local people present, the police write a report on the apparent cause of death. The report goes to the District or Sub-divisional Magistrate within 24 hours.
official.confirms: BNSS Section 194(1) and 194(2): investigation "in the presence of two or more respectable inhabitants"; report forwarded "within twenty-four hours".

official.text: If there is any doubt about the cause of death, the police can send the body to a government doctor for a medical examination, also called a post-mortem.
official.confirms: BNSS Section 194(3)(iv) and (v): where "there is any doubt regarding the cause of death", forward the body "to the nearest Civil Surgeon, or other qualified medical person".

official.text: When a woman dies within seven years of her marriage, a relative can ask for this medical examination.
official.confirms: BNSS Section 194(3)(iii): death of a woman within seven years of marriage "and any relative of the woman has made a request in this behalf".

official.text: For LIC's accident benefit, papers like the FIR and the post-mortem report are normally asked for.
official.confirms: LIC claims requirements, Double Accident Benefit Claims: "documents like FIR, Post-mortem Report are insisted upon".

suggestions: Ask the police station handling the case how to get copies of the FIR, the inquest report and the post-mortem report. Insurers and banks may ask for them.
Make sure the death is registered. The page "If the death certificate is not ready" explains how.
It is fine to ask a friend or relative to go to the police station with you.
lawyer: You think someone caused the death, or you disagree with the police report.
